title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering during regional failover
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Hotfix: Fixes SLO enforcer backoff ordering bug that could cause excessive load-shedding during regional failover; improves smoothing and adds regression tests; safe to roll out immediately.
description: Context: During the 2026-02-25 regional failover incident we observed the SLO enforcer enter a thrashing state where multiple backoff timers were applied out-of-order causing aggressive, repeated load-shedding and unnecessary cross-region failovers. Root cause: a race between the backoff timer update path and the route-switch path during failover which could leave an enforcer instance with stale pendingBackoff state and then apply a second backoff when the new route became active. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes and transient 5xxs for some high-throughput customers. This PR fixes the ordering bug and hardens the enforcer to avoid double-shedding during regional failover. Changes: 1) Reorder state transitions in src/slo/enforcer.go so that route-switch completes before any backoff enqueueing; 2) Add an atomic backoff guard (pending_backoff_id) and make backoff application idempotent; 3) Tighten threshold smoothing window to reduce oscillation during rapid failovers; 4) Add unit and integration regression tests that reproduce the backoff ordering sequence; 5) Add a short-lived metric (slo_enforcer.backoff_double_apply_count) + alert query to detect regressions; 6) Add a canary rollout job in ci/canary/slo-enforcer-canary.yml. Testing: Unit tests added and pass locally; integration test simulates cross-region failover and asserts only a single backoff applied; CI initially showed an intermittent integration failure, re-run succeeded; deployed to canary region us-west-2 for 30m with no regressions observed. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main and promote to release pipeline; canary for 1h in us-west-2 then gradual 10/30/60 rollout to remaining regions with metrics monitoring. Notes: This change is intentionally conservative (no behavioral change to backoff policy) aside from ordering/idempotency; no customer-facing API changes. Linked: ENG-3245 for post-incident work and SUP-1189 for customer impact tracking.
